title: Comparison: Supreme Court vs High Court

blocks.content: The writ jurisdiction of the High Court under Article 226 is wider than that of the Supreme Court under Article 32.

rows: Barred from practicing in any court in India
Can practice in SC and other High Courts

items: Article 32 is itself a Fundamental Right, so the Supreme Court cannot refuse to exercise its writ jurisdiction, whereas Article 226 is discretionary for High Courts.
High Courts have power of superintendence over all courts and tribunals within their territorial jurisdiction, except military tribunals.
A retired High Court judge can practice only in the Supreme Court and other High Courts where they have not served as a permanent judge, whereas SC judges cannot practice in any court in India.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Supreme Court is the apex court of the nation established under Article 124, while High Courts operate at the state level under Article 214.
The writ jurisdiction of High Courts (Article 226) is broader than that of the Supreme Court (Article 32), as High Courts can issue writs for both Fundamental Rights and legal rights.
Judges of both the Supreme Court and High Courts are appointed by the President of India.
The Supreme Court judge holds office until the age of 65 years, whereas a High Court judge holds office until the age of 62 years.
The Supreme Court possesses original, appellate, advisory, and special leave jurisdictions, making its decisions binding on all courts across India.
